name: gizza-ai/protobuf-decode
summary: Decode raw protobuf wire bytes into a field/wire-type tree without a .proto schema.

tool.description: Decode raw Protocol Buffers (protobuf) wire bytes into a field-number / wire-type tree WITHOUT a .proto schema. Give the wire bytes as base64 or hex in 'input' (set encoding='auto' (default), 'base64', or 'hex'). Each field is reported by its field number, raw wire type (varint / fixed32 / fixed64 / length_delimited) and every plausible interpretation, since the schemaless wire format is ambiguous: a varint is shown as uint/int/zigzag (and bool when 0/1); fixed32 as uint32/int32/float; fixed64 as uint64/int64/double; a length-delimited field is recursively parsed as a nested message when it parses cleanly, and also shown as a string (when valid text) and as hex bytes. Use format='json' (default) for a structured tree or 'text' for a compact outline. Useful for reverse-engineering an undocumented gRPC / protobuf payload.

encoding.description: How the input bytes are encoded. 'auto' (default) detects hex (only hex digits, even length) else base64. base64 accepts standard or URL-safe, padding optional; hex ignores spaces, ':' and '-'.

format.description: Output shape. 'json' (default) is a structured tree of {field, wire_type, ...interpretations}; 'text' is a compact indented outline.

input.description: The raw protobuf wire bytes, as a base64 or hex string.
